title: Route traffic through a Google Cloud failure
description: Select a healthy path, a zonal loss, or a regional loss. The active route, failed boundary, component responsibility, and user-visible result change together.

nodes.label: User request
nodes.detail: The user needs the complete business journey, not merely a successful edge connection.

nodes.label: Global load balancer
nodes.detail: The global edge applies policy and chooses a healthy backend. Its health signal must test the dependency path required for service.

nodes.label: Primary zone A
nodes.detail: Cloud Run capacity, GKE workloads, or a managed instance group serves one placement slice. It must be disposable without losing authority.

nodes.label: Primary zone B
nodes.detail: Independent zonal capacity carries the full admitted peak after one zone is removed, including retry and rollout pressure.

nodes.label: Regional data authority
nodes.detail: A zonally resilient database can preserve regional availability. Its transaction, connection, backup, and failover behavior still needs workload validation.

nodes.label: Secondary region
nodes.detail: A regional target is useful only when it is deployed, authorized, reachable, within quota, and scaled for the recovery objective.

nodes.label: Secondary data copy
nodes.detail: Cross-region state needs a known replication position, promotion authority, conflict policy, restore evidence, and safe failback procedure.

scenarios.label: Healthy region
scenarios.summary: Both primary zones serve traffic and share a regional data authority while recovery state replicates asynchronously.
scenarios.result: The regional path is available. The secondary data copy improves recoverability, but it is not a second serving region without compute, routing, quota, and promotion controls.

scenarios.label: Zone A fails
scenarios.summary: The edge removes zone A. Zone B and the regional data service must absorb peak traffic without waiting for new capacity.
scenarios.result: Requests continue only if the surviving zone, database, connections, and quotas were sized for failover. Extra replicas in the failed zone would not help.

scenarios.label: Primary region fails
scenarios.summary: Primary compute and data authority are unavailable. Global routing can use the secondary only after its complete serving contract is ready.
scenarios.result: Regional recovery succeeds only after the secondary proves health, capacity, IAM, dependency reachability, and an accepted data position. Operators must fence the old writer before promotion.
